messages:
alicia: quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide how hetero-prefetch interacts with NUMA affinity + eviction fairness across tenants. Draft proposal below.

ben: +1. can you summarize the options?

alicia: options:
1) strict-local: always prefetch into local NUMA socket and prefer local eviction pressure
2) soft-local: prefer local but allow remote spill if local pressure > burst_threshold
3) pooled-host: prefetch into host staging (non-GPU) for low memory models, keep GPU for hot KV cache
tradeoffs: strict-local = best latency but fragmentation & imbalance; pooled-host = better global fairness but higher tail latency

chandra: we need metrics to choose thresholds. suggest tracking per-tenant hotset-residence, prefetch-hit-rate, tail-p99 latency, and fragmentation-% by socket

alicia: yeah proposed telemetry keys: resident_bytes_by_socket, prefetch_p95_latency_ms, demote_events, eviction_reassigns

diane: rollout plan? we can't flip any global flag. need per-tenant policy + canary percent and throttled ramp. existing rollout hooks in console ok? :thinking_face:

alicia: exactly. config snippet:
```
tenant_policies:
  tenant_id:
    prefetch:
      mode: soft-local
      local_burst_threshold_mb: 512
      demote_threshold_ms: 300
      numa_preference: 'local'
      spill_target: 'host-staging'
```

ben: ok but interface question: should runtime expose a 'residency_score' API on allocations, or should prefetcher compute heuristics independently?

chandra: residency_score makes sense for orthogonal components (evictor, prefetcher, admission) to share signal. score in [0,100] and monotonic.

sam: watch out: computing score synchronously on alloc path could add latency. compute async or sample-based. prefer per-epoch aggregator.

alicia: agreed. plan: residency_score produced by sampler thread every 100ms per page-range. exporter tags pages with score.

diane: adaptive fairness: propose fair-share demote: when pressure high, pick victim tenants with highest overbudget = resident/commit_ratio, not just oldest pages

ben: implement as two-stage: calculate tenant_overload = resident_bytes / committed_bytes, then weight eviction probability by overload^alpha

chandra: tune alpha based on experiments. also add a safety cap so single tenant can't be demoted below min_resident for latency-sensitive models

alicia: perf tests to run:
- single-tenant low-memory model under strict-local
- multi-tenant mixed (small/large) with pooled-host
- flame graphs + tail-latency p99cap
run script:
```
./scripts/run_prefetch_experiment.sh --scenario mixed --duration 10m --collect=resident_by_socket,latency_hist
```

diane: CI check: deploy-bot reports branch build ok but integration tests flaky on NUMA machines

deploy-bot: build/4321 passed, integ/numa-tests failed on 2/8 runs (OOM on host-staging). Logs: https://ci/reports/4321

alicia: ack. next steps: (1) add residency_score proto + exporter (2) add per-tenant config + console flags (3) run perf suite and iterate alpha, thresholds (4) small canary with 5% traffic

ben: I can take residency_score proto + sampler

chandra: I'll own eviction weighting + metrics

diane: I'll wire console rollout + canary automation

sam: I'll triage CI flakes and repro host-staging OOMs

alicia: thanks. tiny open Q: should we expose per-page numa_hint vs per-range? prefer range-level to limit metadata overhead

chandra: range-level only. per-page too heavy.

ben: agreed.

alicia: cool. I'll update the RFC doc and post link later :sparkles:
